official.deadline_note: No central deadline is published: the programme page gives the due date as 'Continuous' and states that intake open dates are specific to each individual university - applicants must contact their university for deadline information (page 11 of the Program Guidelines lists the institutional contacts).
official.application_cycle: Continuous at the funder level; seasonal intake at each participating institution
official.status_note: Alberta Innovates publishes Programme Status: Active and Intake Status: Open, stating that the programme is accepting applications on a seasonal basis with intake dates specific to each university.
benefits: Scholarship funding enabling full-time graduate students to devote their full time to their academic studies
Funding ranging from $12,000 to $31,000 per year, with terms of one to four years depending on the recipient's time in the programme
Open to Canadian citizens, permanent residents and international students
Multi-year scholarships renewed annually after the first year upon satisfactory reporting by the student
eligibility: Be a Canadian citizen, a permanent resident of Canada, or an international student

Be enrolled as a full-time graduate student conducting full-time research at a participating institution: Athabasca University, Concordia University of Edmonton, the University of Alberta, the University of Calgary or the University of Lethbridge
Be conducting research in key emerging technology areas of information and communications technologies (ICT) or advanced materials and manufacturing technologies (AMM)
Meet the eligibility requirements in the terms of reference of the award at the time the award is paid, even if they were not met at application
requirements: Check with your institution's faculty of graduate studies for full descriptions and application details
Submit your application to your institution - the applicant does not apply directly to Alberta Innovates
Review the programme guidelines before applying; awards are based on merit
selection_criteria: Each participating institution has its own scholarship application and evaluation processes for students in full-time programmes; Alberta Innovates directs applicants to their faculty of graduate studies for that information
Awards are based on merit; students must read and understand the terms of reference
coverage: Funding ranging from $12,000 to $31,000 per year, with terms varying from one to four years depending on the recipient's time in the programme
Researchers must complete annual and final reports through the term of the award and post-award reports after the award ends
application_method: Check with your institution's faculty of graduate studies for the full description and application details
Submit your application to your institution
Wait for your application to be reviewed by that institution
official.application_route: Institution-mediated: apply through your own university's graduate awards process - Alberta Innovates itself accepts no direct applications and publishes only 'Continuous' as its due date.
official.study_mode: Full-time graduate study and full-time research
official.citizenship_residency: Canadian citizens, permanent residents of Canada, or international students at one of the five participating Alberta institutions
official.international_eligibility: Yes - international students are explicitly eligible
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Research in key emerging technology areas of ICT or advanced materials and manufacturing technologies, aligned with Alberta Innovates' applied digital and emerging technology areas, with potential environmental, health, economic, social and other impacts for Alberta
official.research_requirement: Full-time research at a participating institution in ICT or AMM emerging technology areas; the work should develop rather than merely use an emerging technology and articulate impact for Alberta
official.duration: Terms vary from one to four years, depending on the recipient's time in the programme; multi-year awards are renewed annually after the first year upon satisfactory reporting
official.description: The Alberta Innovates Graduate Student Scholarships programme provides funding ranging from $12,000 to $31,000 per year to enable full-time graduate students - Canadian, permanent resident or international - to research emerging technologies at participating Alberta post-secondary institutions, in the key emerging technology areas of information and communications technologies and advanced materials and manufacturing technologies.
official.program_type: Government scholarship (Alberta Innovates, delivered through participating post-secondary institutions)

applicant_utility.summary: You never apply to Alberta Innovates - you apply through your own institution's graduate awards competition, so the deadline that matters is your university's internal one (for example, the University of Calgary's Graduate Award Competition opens November 1 each year, with a Faculty of Graduate Studies reference date of February 1 and programme-level variation). The research frame is the make-or-break element: the work must sit in ICT or advanced materials and manufacturing, develop rather than merely use an emerging technology, and articulate concrete environmental, health, economic or social impact for Alberta. International students are eligible on the same footing as domestic students, which is unusual and worth exploiting.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Full-time thesis-based master's and doctoral students at the University of Alberta, Calgary, Lethbridge, Athabasca or Concordia of Edmonton whose research develops an emerging ICT or advanced-materials technology with an Alberta impact story.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your institution is one of the five participating universities and find its internal awards competition deadline - do not wait for Alberta Innovates
Frame your project against Alberta Innovates' applied digital and emerging technology areas document, explicitly developing (not just applying) a technology
Write the Alberta impact case: environmental, health, economic, social or other impacts for the province
Read the award's terms of reference early - eligibility is assessed against them at payment time, not only at application
Request and track references through your institution's system so they land by the internal deadline; admission references written within the prior eleven months can often be reused
common_rejection_risks: Applying directly to Alberta Innovates instead of through the institution, which is not accepted
Missing the institution's internal deadline while relying on the funder's 'Continuous' label
A project that uses emerging technology without developing it, or without a credible Alberta impact claim
Being in a course-based or professional programme where the institution's graduate award competition excludes it
Failing to meet the terms-of-reference conditions by the time the award is paid, which voids eligibility even after selection
Forgetting that multi-year renewal depends on satisfactory annual and final reporting
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The published range is $12,000 to $31,000 per year with one-to-four-year terms; the official page does not state what the funding covers, so tuition, living costs and travel should be assumed to remain the student's responsibility unless the institution's award letter says otherwise.
document_audit: Alberta Innovates publishes no document list - your faculty of graduate studies defines the required forms and reference process, so get their checklist rather than a generic one
Transcripts are uploaded to the application by your programme, so make sure your programme office has them before the internal deadline
Institutional rules differ - for example at the University of Calgary you must hold a UCID from your admissions application before you can apply for graduate funding
alerts: Only one Graduate Award Competition application is normally needed regardless of how many awards you are pursuing - check your institution's rules before submitting duplicates
Successful students must complete annual, final and post-award reports; renewal after year one depends on satisfactory reporting

Institutional category values within the $12,000-$31,000 range (for example $26,000 master's and $31,000 doctoral at the University of Calgary) are set by the university, not the funder - confirm the current figures with your institution
Eligibility is tested again at payment time, so keep your full-time enrolment and research status clean through the award
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Institutional application through your faculty of graduate studies (for example the University of Calgary's Graduate Award Competition from November 1), with references tracked in-system and transcripts uploaded by the programme; the institution reviews and nominates, and Alberta Innovates pays through the institution.
